notes.title: 1.0.5 - The 'First Class' Update is here!
notes.notes:
Major Update! 
Hey everyone! we’re excited to announce The First Class Update is now live! This major quality-of-life update adds additional polish and some final touches, based on player feedback we've received since launch!

To celebrate, we’re offering our deepest discount yet. From 2nd - 9th June, Loco Motive is 20% off! 
Tell your friends, your heirs, and any sworn adversaries!

There’s never been a better time to play, so climb aboard! You’ll be playing the most refined version of Loco Motive to date, complete with extra polish and optimisations designed to enhance your experience.

You can find a full rundown of the patch notes below, but here's a brief overview:

Update Overview

 Refined puzzle logic, for smoother gameplay across key chapters
 Improvements to UI, such as mouse wheel scrolling in the inventory!
 Numerous bugs squashed, enhancing overall stability and player experience
 Additional polish, to animations, environment visuals, and more!
 English (US) localisation introduced, alongside the existing English (UK) version
 Overhauled Autosave system, improving performance and reliability

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d08f1cb466e983a35fd85f4dbb6e03f0d1c722dd.png

MCV/Develop Awards 

Great news, folks! We’ve been shortlisted for Visual Innovation of the Year in the upcoming 2025 MCV/DEVELOP Awards, taking place in London, UK on June 19, 2025. 

The MCV/DEVELOP Awards have been around for over 20 years, and aim to recognise the successes of the UK games industry in every area that it excels. We worked on Loco Motive for close to four years, so it’s immensely cool to be recognised by our peers, and to be nominated alongside some incredible titles. Fingers crossed and best of luck to everybody!

You can check out the full shortlist here.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/c3a7ed0caa65576f3ef37f34e2ce0165b61b5c6f.jpg

New Milestone Reached!

We've crunched the numbers and we're so excited to share that Loco Motive has now sold over 30,000 copies across PC and Nintendo Switch. This is a huge milestone for a small team like ours, especially with our debut title. It truly means the world to us. If you played Loco Motive at launch, told a friend about us, or even spread the word on socials, then we couldn’t have reached this point without you! Thank you so much for your continued feedback, passion, and support!

Without further ado, here’s the spoiler-free nitty gritty of this update…

1.0.5 - Full Patch Notes

Lady Unterwald Quarters

The Green Room

Engine Room

UI

notes.title: Patch 1.0.4 is OUT!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone!

We really appreciate your passion and support since the launch—it means a lot to us. Patch 1.0.4 is now live on PC and Nintendo Switch* - This is our first update, and it addresses many of the bugs and issues you've reported since release. 

*(17/12/2024) The patch is now available on Nintendo Switch, thank you for your patience!

Thanks to all of your helpful feedback and reports, we believe we’ve pinpointed the cause of the soft-locking issues. These should now be resolved, and we can’t thank you enough for your patience while we worked on these fixes!

Here’s a rundown of the changes:

[STABILITY]


 fixed soft locks caused by incorrect handling of cancelled interactions
 fixed soft lock that could occur when clicking multiple times on don's broken door
 fixed rare soft lock when interacting with sister Gretchen and brother Jared in chapter two
 fixed soft lock where the band could get stuck in a loop when entering green room in chapter four
 fixed threading issue that could occur when interacting with the band members
 fixed soft lock that could occur when rapidly clicking on the casino patrons
 fixed potential threading issues when showing the perfumed note to characters
 fixed threading issue when talking to the highrollers in the casino
 fixed potential threading issues when leaving dialogue trees
 fixed soft lock due to erroneous character positioning during chapter six
 fixed threading issues when interacting with characters whilst drunk
 fixed a crash on certain windows system languages when looking at the medical records
 fixed null reference exception when an active controller is disconnected due to low battery
 fixed background sequences being stopped when an interaction is cancelled
 fixed soft lock when loading into chapter six from an autosave
 fixed a soft lock when talking to the chefs in chapter three
 fixed threading issues during unhandled fall-back interactions with characters, inventory items & props
 fixed soft lock when giving the briefcase to the twins in chapter two

[DIALOGUE]

 fixed german eszett character not appearing for lines displayed in all caps
 fixed dialogue text rendering off screen when using certain settings
 fixed issue where Lady Unterwald displayed incorrect dialogue options at beginning of chapter four
 fixed subtitle dialogue continuing to show after the twins escape from the vent in chapter four
 fixed accessibility text settings not being applied to background sequence dialogue

[VISUAL]

 fixed doctor Hirsch being very shy and facing the wall during handshake cutscenes in chapter four
 fixed Diana rendering underneath the motorbike in the test yard
 fixed Don remaining invisible if you leave the casino without following him
 fixed visual bug when showing Ron the detective badge at the dining table
 fixed the quartermaster from disappearing when using the hint line in the test yard
 fixed issue where Herman could show the detective badge to characters while in disguise
 fixed visual issues when giving the briefcase to the twins in chapter two
 fixed visual issues when giving the sketches to doctor Hirsch in chapter two
 fixed Philately Stamp visual issues during the mansion lobby cutscene in the finale 
 fixed issue where Don appeared in the post credits cutscene

[GAMEPLAY]

 added specific calls for combining the various knife state items with the slippery mixture
 fixed Arthur not walking towards brother Jared when interacting whilst drunk
 fixed Arthur not walking towards Belle when giving her an item
 fixed suction boots remaining active when using them on the ladder in chapter four
 fixed incendiary pencils remaining active when using them on the firebox in chapter five
 fixed hearing horn background sequence continuing when leaving the room
 fixed Don's betting sequence being triggered if you enter the casino whilst he's leaving for the dining carriage
 fixed Don and Bergmann background sequence continuing when leaving the room
 fixed publisher pigeon background sequence continuing when looking at the in-tray

[SAVES]

 fix for save states affected by erroneous character positioning in chapter six
 fixed handshake club lights issue on initial autosave after Arthur drinks the rosebud
 fixed autosave icon not disappearing if an action was cancelled by the player

[UI]

 updated credits list
 fixed the console being accessible on release builds
 fixed tutorial popups not disappearing if an action was cancelled by the player


We encourage you to keep sharing your feedback and thoughts on forums and social media. We’re actively reading your comments and taking note of areas where we can improve in future updates. If you come across any more issues, please report them! This helps us investigate your specific case and implement fixes more quickly.

Thank you so much for your continued feedback, passion, and support during this time!

notes.title: Development Update #13
notes.notes:
🎊Loco Motive is finished!🎊

Let's get straight into it, we've hit our biggest milestone yet! - After several years in development, we're very pleased to confirm that Loco Motive is complete. We'll be continuing to squash any bugs in the lead up to launch, of course, but the work is done. We made an entire video-game, people!

We've had a few questions about whether we are still intending to release Loco Motive in Q4 2024.. 

Yes! we'll be announcing our release date very soon, so please stay tuned for impending updates! 


🎙️Role Call! - Voice Cast Announced🎙️

Earlier last month we gave the green light for our talented voice cast to announce their roles, and they delivered with gusto! Huge thanks to Kimlinh Tran and Kirsty Gilmore for casting! - we're proud to confirm (in Alphabetical order) that Loco Motive features the vocal talents of:

Jack Ayres as Gunter Gudrun, Hagen Gudrun, Jimmy

Jack is a Welsh actor and Voice Actor originally from Cardiff, South Wales. Jack has established himself as a versatile and rising voice actor for video games and character voices having featured in almost 40 video game titles as of 2024, including Baldur’s Gate III and Black Myth: Wukong.

Samantha Béart as April Benelli

Samantha is a BAFTA and DICE nominated, GANG Award-winning actor. In the world of videogames, they are best known for their role as Karlach in Baldur’s Gate III, but you may also know them as Thomasina in the critically acclaimed adventure game “The Excavation of Hob’s Barrow”.

Sally Beaumont as Beverly Moore, Sister Gretchen, Quinn Morgan, Florence Schreiber, Pearl Wexler, Shelly Gedling 

Sally is a voice actor living in Oxford, UK and no stranger to voicing adventure game characters, having played a wide range across 30+ video game titles. This includes The Excavation of Hob's Barrow, a leading role as Fia in the upcoming Old Skies, and a stand out performance as Weeoo in Harold Halibut.

Alasdair Beckett-King as The Handshake Leader

Alasdair is an author, actor, video game writer and award-winning stand-up comedian, winner of the 2017 Leicester Mercury Comedian of the Year, and Chortle's Breakthrough Comedian of the Year in 2023. Alasdair is also the creator of the Nelly Cootalot series of adventure games.

Sean Chiplock as Arthur Ackerman

Sean has been an avid participant in videogame culture ever since his childhood, so it’s no surprise that he enjoys performing for them just as much as he enjoys playing them. In the world of videogames, Sean has featured in everything from AAA behemoths like The Legend of Zelda: Breath of the Wild and Genshin Impact to indie success stories such as the recent Duck Detective: The Secret Salami.

Savy Des-Etages as Diana Osterhagen

Savy is an experienced voice actor and audiobook narrator hailing from Lancashire, UK. In the world of video games, Savy has lent her talents to widely popular titles such as Viewfinder, Cassette Beasts, Fallout: London and more!

Antonio Greco as Donny Donato, Casino Enforcer 

Antonio is a versatile voice actor who specialises in character, animation / cartoon, and video game character voices.

Darius T Jackson as Raymond, Sonny, Victor

Darius is a Chicago based voice actor for video games and animations, known for their role as Felix in Cassette Beasts.

Jacob Janerka as Brother Jared

Once described as Australia's ‘most enigmatic’ game developer, Jacob Janerka is known as the creator of the surreal adventure game Paradigm and the upcoming The Dungeon Experience. 

Dave Jones as Lex Lamont, Isaac, Harold

Dave has previously voiced characters in video games such as The Excavation of Hob's Barrow and Planet Zoo, but he is perhaps best known for his role as Halsin in Baldur’s Gate III. This performance earned him a spot on the BAFTA Game Awards longlist for- Best Performance in a Supporting Role.

Amina Koroma as Justice Bailey, Edna, Doris

Based in South London, Amina is co-founder of the British VO Network and a talented voice over artist who reads across Commercials, Drama, Animation and Gaming. In the field of video games, Amina is known for their roles in Baldur’s Gate III and Read Only Memories: Neurodiver.

Nickeem Latty-Morgan as Emmanuel, Sonny

Nickeem is a voice actor and freelance video editor based in South London, specialising in character performances for video games and animation.

Jim Meskimen as Mr Masson

James Ross "Jim" Meskimen is an accomplished actor, impressionist and voice actor who has been a fixture in film, TV, animation, games and audiobooks for decades. He has appeared in films for director Ron Howard, Paul Thomas Anderson and Garry Marshall.

Brent Mukai as Herman Merman

Brent is a Japanese American Voice Actor, based in Los Angeles. He brings a decade of experience in film and theatre acting, improv comedy, and stand up comedy. Brent is known in games for his roles in Ratchet and Clank: Rift Apart, Genshin Impact, Lost Judgement and Fire Emblem Warriors: Three Hopes

André Refig as Antoine Cassoulet

André is a dual-nationality French-British actor based in London, UK, and has provided a wide range of voices for video game projects from indies to AAAs in both English and French. André is known for their role as Aymeric Cassel in Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty

Will Derenzy-Martin as Doctor Hirsch, Kasper Bergmann, François Tatin, Philately Stamp, Maurice

Will is an award-Winning Voice Actor based in London, UK. Will has played a wide range of characters, including Hercule Poirot in Hercule Poirot: The First Cases and Milil (God of Song) in Baldur's Gate III. Other titles include Black Myth: Wukong and The Excavation of Hob's Barrow.

Maxim Reston as Remy Galette

Maxim is an experienced multilingual British voice artist and actor based in London, UK. They have featured in a number of video games such as Dragon Quest Monsters: The Dark Prince, Banishers: Ghosts of New Eden and Jagged Alliance 3.

Kaitlyn Robrock as Lady Unterwald, Arista Gudrun 

Kaitlyn is an American voice actress, best known for her role as the current voice of Disney’s Minnie Mouse. She is also known for her role as Felicia Sundew on Disney’s Amphibia and Tommy Goodman on Adult Swim’s Mr. Pickles.

Leonie Schliesing as the Shoeshine Girl

Leonie is a multilingual, award winning Voice Actor. Their videogame roles include Aurore Cassel in Cyberpunk 2077: Phantom Liberty and Toka in Assassins’ Creed: Valhalla.  

Edwyn Tiong as Jian Liu, Frank 

Edwyn is a Voice Actor and writer based in Adelaide, Australia. They have featured in a wide range of video games, including Cassette Beasts, Harold Halibut, Unavowed and Freedom Planet 2. They are also known for their role as Detective Grimoire in Tangle Tower and its upcoming sequel, The Mermaid Mask.

Inel Tomlinson as Dirk Chiselton

Inel is an actor, TV personality and stand-up comedian from London, UK. Inel is a main cast member in the smash hit show Horrible Histories, he also hosts for Comic Con, BAFTA, Netflix and is the voice of Comedy Central UK. Inel has also voiced for a number of video games, including Final Fantasy XVI and Warhammer 40,000: Space Marine II.

Adrian Vaughan as The Board, Byron, Thomas Page, Ron, Henry Whistle, Vince Fortune, Brother Brian 

Adrian is a voice actor based in Melbourne, Australia. Their voice features in a wide range of video games, including Wargroove, Harold Halibut, Budget Cuts and upcoming adventure game, The Drifter.

Natalie Winter as Susanne Goldschmidt, Ruth, Evelyn, Mary

Natalie is a UK based Voice Actor and Director, with credits spanning stage, screen, games, and radio. She has voiced a number of video games, including Assassins’ Creed: Valhalla, Skull and Bones, and The Excavation Of Hobbs Barrow.


🌟Next Fest Post-Mortem🌟

The dust has finally settled on Steam Next Fest, and we couldn't be happier with the response to the demo! thank you to everyone who played, streamed on Twitch, told a friend and provided feedback! 

Loco Motive was in the top 50 titles under the 'Most Wishlisted Upcoming Games' tab, meaning we featured in the top 1.41% of all games that participated!

We also did very well in our chosen categories, with Loco Motive featuring as the #1 game in the Point-And-Click and Investigation categories, and charting #2 in Comedy, #3 in Mystery and #4 in the Puzzle categories.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/208d81a068f176c74aa649059d50bf791edf1835.png

We also received some kind words in the Press, of which we've curated a few quotes:


 "If you're a LucasArts nut or just like a witty murder mystery, Loco Motive is a must play.... The set-up, characters, pixel art, slapstick humor, voice acting, animation – everything is fantastic." - GamesRadar+

 "I really recommend checking out Loco Motive. When people say "LucasArts-style adventure" they normally wildly exaggerate. From this ENORMOUS demo, it might finally be time to bring out the accolade." - John Walker, Co-Creator of Rock Paper Shotgun

 "Loco Motive throws you headlong into a murder mystery worthy of an Agatha Christie novel but with the wit and slapstick of a classic cartoon...The exquisite animation, snappy soundtrack and soundscapes will have you engrossed." - Thumb Culture

 Loco Motive is a throwback adventure game featuring rich characters, lovely sprite art, and plenty of comedy. - PC Mag


🎖️We're nominated in the DevGAMM Awards!🎖️

We're very excited and humbled to announce that Loco Motive has been nominated in three categories at the upcoming DevGAMM Awards 2024 for: 

🏆'EXCELLENCE IN NARRATIVE'
🏆'EXCELLENCE IN VISUAL ART'
🏆'THE GRAND PRIZE' 

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/8fa8d6accee9652f2cc9de70779b114faaf6efc3.png

This was a very welcome surprise, and we'll be eagerly attending in Lisbon, Portugal next week with our fingers and toes crossed! 

✨Wishlists!✨

We're delighted to announce that we're very close to our dream goal of 100,000 wishlists by launch!

Another shout-out to everyone who added Loco Motive to your wishlists, shared feedback and has supported us throughout development. We're a tiny indie team creating our debut game and this means a lot to us! 

If you haven't already, consider wishlisting Loco Motive to receive a notification when the full game launches. It’s just one click, but it really helps us out!

https://store.steampowered.com/app/1709880/

Stay tuned for impending news, you can follow us for regular updates on Twitter or join the official Robust Games Discord.

notes.title: Development Update #12
notes.notes:
Hey, everyone!

It’s been a little while since our last development update, and wow, time really flies! 
We’ve admittedly been a bit quiet, but that’s only because we’ve been fully heads down and pushing to get the game completed and as polished as possible. That said...

🎊Content Complete!🎊

We’re thrilled to announce another major milestone: Loco Motive is content complete! For the past month, we’ve been fully focused on polishing and bug fixing, making sure every aspect of the game meets our quality standards, and ensuring nothing is overlooked. With the end of development fast approaching, our next milestone is to have a completed build that we can comfortably call a Release Candidate.

In order to help us reach this stage, a dedicated QA team and our volunteer internal testers have been playing through the game in both English and German, providing feedback and helping us to locate and squash any bugs we might have missed!

⏱️Time to Completion⏱️

Based on early playtime feedback from our testers, I can comfortably call Loco Motive a feature-length experience, with an average playtime of around 14-15 hours. There's a lot of content here! 

📺We were on the telly!📺

This was a weird one, but we were shocked to see Loco Motive feature as a question on the hugely popular UK quiz show, The Chase!

Thanks for getting it right, Jan!

We're delighted to announce we've hit another wishlist milestone. Thanks to your support, we recently reached over 90,000 outstanding wishlists! 

Another huge shout-out to you all for adding Loco Motive to your wishlists, sharing feedback and supporting us throughout our development so far. We're a tiny indie team creating our debut game and this means a lot to us! This gets us closer to our dream goal of 100,000 wishlists by launch!

notes.title: Development Update #11
notes.notes:
Hi there!

It’s been another busy few months for the Loco Motive team as we reach the end stages of development, but we're eager to bring you up to speed! 

Voice Acting Complete!

Another huge milestone has been reached, as we've now completed all of our recording sessions for the game. All 8000+ lines of dialogue have been implemented, and we're currently processing each line to ensure everything is of a consistent quality and volume level, etc.

We'll be holding off on any casting announcements just a little longer, but we could not be happier with the ensemble we've put together! The final roster features a whopping 23 talented voice artists, who'll be voicing our cast of 60+ characters!

[center][table][tr][td]
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/37e115ccef76b05757c3c291b800b367786953f4.jpg[/td][/tr][/table][/center]

Final Assets

Over the next few weeks, our priority is to get the remaining art and animation into the last chapter of the game, along with any remaining sound effects and music. It's been super satisfying to see that list get shorter every day. Once we reach the content complete stage, we'll be adding the final touches of polish and focusing on squashing any remaining bugs!

Close-ups

One of the elements we've been working on adding periodically throughout the game are close-up shots, which will appear during dramatic moments or to add better context to the narrative. 

Close-ups begin as illustrated sketches by the wonderfully talented Loukia Kyriakidou, who also illustrated our key art and characters!

notes.title: Development Update #10
notes.notes:
“Hallo Freunde!”

It’s been a busy few months for the Loco Motive team, but we're eager to bring you up to speed on our latest developments! Since our last update, we've been busy recording voice-over dialogue with our cast, forging exciting new partnerships, and approaching a significant milestone: Finalising all the text in the game!

The writing process involved plenty of typing, ruminating and head-scratching but after 70,000 words or so - I'm glad to say we're almost there. As we worked towards this milestone, it enabled us to better explore our options with localisation. 

The adventure game community is known for a strong and loyal German following, and Loco Motive has been no exception. With Germany featuring prominently as a top wishlist region, this was an easy decision for us to make:

✨We're delighted to announce that Loco Motive will be launching with German language support!✨

We’ve teamed up with Marcel Weyers to create the German localisation for Loco Motive, who you may be familiar with for their work on Return To Monkey Island, Goodbye Volcano High & Coffee Talk: Episode 2! 

Marcel was happy to share a few words about the project:

“Working on Loco Motive has been super fun! There's so much attention to detail in this project, and even though some of the puns were quite tricky to translate, I can't wait for German adventure gamers to be able to play the game and laugh out loud as much as I did!”

notes.title: Development Update #9 - 2023 Recap!
notes.notes:
Hello there! It's time for the last Loco Motive blog of the year, so let's get straight to it!

As I write this blog post, we’re winding down development here and preparing to spend some well earned time with our family over the Christmas holidays. It’s a time of reflection, so let’s look at all we’ve achieved, and what’s left to come for us in the new year!

🧭2023 Recap🧭

2023! It’s been a year of highlights, but let’s look at some of our biggest milestones:


 We demoed at PAX East and EGX 2023 - the UK's biggest gaming exhibition!
 The game became ‘fully playable’ from start to finish
 Loco Motive was nominated for a Critics’ Choice Award
 We were officially selected to be part of LudoNarracon 2023
 We debuted our first playable demo on Steam as part of Steam Mystery Fest
 Full controller support was added to the game!
 We reached over 70,000+ Wishlists!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/1c3aa8ebdab3448bfdc5c727fa66d54a2ae1a338.jpg

But that’s not all! We had time to squeeze in just a few more things before our Christmas break..

🎤 Voice Acting has begun!🎤 

Many of the questions we’ve received so far have revolved around voice, and if / when Loco Motive will feature voice acting.

I am pleased to confirm that we've recently begun recording dialogue with a professional voice cast, who we couldn’t be more excited about! These talented voice actors have featured in games such as The Legend Of Zelda: Tears Of The Kingdom, Viewfinder, Genshin Impact, Baldur’s Gate III, Starfield and more!

We’ll be announcing the full cast as we record more dialogue and get closer to launch, so keep your eyes peeled for a future announcement. Until then, we'll be keeping you guessing!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/cb2424a1d3614dd48ebe008d9d3589ede18c5c23.png

⚙️Accessibility Options!⚙️

We wanted Loco Motive to be more accessible and give players more options. We recently spent some time adding accessibility features to the game, including the following:


 ⏪ Subtitle Speed Settings
 🗨️ Subtitle Backing Settings
  🗚  Bigger Text Size Settings
 📛 Display Speaker Name Option
 📑 Dyslexic Friendly Font Option
 🎉 Confetti Mode! (Removes Blood!)
 🎮 Playstation Controller Support!


Here are some new screenshots to show some of these options in action!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/bf9f31ae70639e119e1f50df28b451c9e720c50c.png

This isn’t an exhaustive list, but we intend to listen to feedback and work to make the game as accessible as we can for launch!

🛠️Development continues!🛠️

Loco Motive became fully playable from start to finish in late July, and since then we've all been working dilligently to get more of the written dialogue into the game, adding more music and SFX, polishing the visuals and adding more animation! We've also been able to start exploring those bigger features like voice acting and localisation. 

We don't want to give too much away just yet, but we thought we could share some brand new animation work from the game for now!

📅Loco Motive launches in 2024📅

As we mentioned earlier this year, Loco Motive will now be launching in 2024 for PC and Nintendo Switch.

notes.title: Development Update #5
notes.notes:
Hello and happy winter! We hope you and your loved ones are staying warm and enjoying the season.

We're excited to report that development is going well, with us recently reaching a significant milestone in the project! We’ll have more to share on that in the new year, so let’s do a little post mortem!

It's been a little over a month since we showcased Loco Motive at AdventureX in London. This was the first time we exhibited the game, and we wanted to share our experience, describe what went well, and look at what could be improved upon.

First, we want to thank everyone who attended the event and provided feedback on our game. We're taking your comments and suggestions to heart!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/d45376c22602e6c2f0bd58c7ff02ce6b07dc13e9.png

During AdventureX, we confirmed that the UK narrative game community is full of supportive and welcoming people. As newcomers to the scene, it was clear that everyone wanted each other to succeed. 
We met many developers and industry veterans who came to the booth and shared their thoughts, ideas and advice with us.

We’re happy to share that people are very excited for Loco Motive! There were often lines of people waiting to play the game during the event, and many attendees came by afterwards to tell us how much they enjoyed it.

Overall, we had a great response and generated a lot of positive buzz. We believe this was due to the game being well-received at the event, word-of-mouth recommendations from other attendees and the fact that we didn't yet have a demo available elsewhere. We're grateful for all the support and feedback we received from those attending!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/a6e6856640225329664b97203f5afe1b567c50ba.png

One area we could improve on in future is the length of the demo. In order to streamline the build, we disabled several puzzle chains in Arthur Ackerman's first act and focused on one overarching puzzle. 

We believed players would get through the demo in around 25-30 minutes, but we noticed they were often spending over an hour in it. This suggests that we could have streamlined things further while still providing a good representation of the game.

In the future, we will likely create a shorter demo. This will help us better manage players' time and provide a more focused experience. Deciding where to end the demo was a challenge for us, but we're confident that we can find a good balance in future iterations.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/3564bc31387cc83a45d6c2db4e0f61883c8bd617.png

We look forward to sharing more updates with you in the coming weeks. In the meantime, we hope you have a wonderful holiday season and a happy new year.

Thank you for your support. We can't wait to share Loco Motive with you!

You can follow us for updates on Twitter or join the official Robust Games Discord.

notes.title: Release Update, Exhibitions & Musical Deep Dive!
notes.notes:
Hey everyone, Adam from Robust Games here. We’re excited to be kicking off another Loco Motive development blog!

Development Update

Before we get into it, we’ve had a few questions about when Loco Motive will be releasing. 

Are we still set for Summer 2022? Isn’t it August already?

So, we've made the decision to delay Loco Motive to 2023.  There are a number of factors behind this decision, but ultimately we believe this extra development time will allow us to deliver the game we want to make and allow Loco Motive to reach its fullest potential.

The excitement surrounding Loco Motive since its reveal in December has been really inspiring, and we appreciate your support so far. 

We hope you’ll stay aboard just a little longer!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/db0ed48567ef57238e8659975968b55de889a29d.png

The Music Of Loco Motive

Our composer, Paul Zimmermann is here to talk about his approach to the music of Loco Motive, and the adaptive system we’ve built around the game as you move between carriages:

"My goal with every project is to find a sound that feels authentic to the game and its characters. 
The soundtrack for Loco Motive is turning out to be this fun blend of different styles and periods in music, from big-band swing to 60s spy music and the occasional French-inspired waltz. 

We have quite the varied cast of characters, so it felt natural to try and reflect that in the music."

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/e1d36c7a6f07fcce2b498792255773d2f59aa4bd.jpg

"From a technical standpoint it was important for us to implement the music into the game in a way that it reacts to the gameplay and locations, opposed to having static looping tracks. 

As players roam around the train trying to solve puzzles, the music follows along and changes seamlessly between carriages and characters."

In order to achieve this, I’m writing and then exporting the music in small chunks that allow for fast transitions, meaning, a certain melody-note might be carried over into the next location, or a groove transitions smoothly. Our thinking here is that if players don’t notice it, then we’ve actually achieved what we set out to do!"

Check out this behind-the-scenes look of how the music system behaves and sounds so far:

We'll have much more music to share as development continues, this is just a taste of what's to come!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/87e4684545c5f2030c78995750a73f7873dd2567.png

AdventureX - The Narrative Games Convention

We’re super excited to announce that Loco Motive has been selected to showcase at AdventureX this year!

AdventureX brings together a wide range of narrative-driven indie games, and is the UK's only convention dedicated to narrative-driven gaming. It's a celebration of creativity, indie development and interactive storytelling, and we’re thrilled to have our game amongst narrative titans. 

The first wave of tickets sold out in just under 20 minutes, so if you’re one of those lucky few, we’ll hopefully see you there!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/efbef6368f65a1d751d745c8cce17317c2c4edc2.jpg

Character Spotlight - Diana Osterhagen

It’s time for our third character spotlight! This time we’re taking a look at our final playable character, the secretive Diana Osterhagen.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/fe261fc59d558a191a2c51525da0b39cdc306ebb.png

Diana is a British operative who's spent the last few months undercover in order to get close to the Unterwald family. 

Tasked with gaining intelligence on potential ‘undeclared assets’, she finds herself aboard the Reuss Express in the arms of Kaspar Bergmann - who just so happens to be the treasurer of Lady Unterwald's wealthy estate. 

Diana is soon swept up in something far more unsettling than undeclared income or tax liabilities, and must use her problem-solving abilities and highly developed interpersonal skills to get out of hot water.
 
{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/cf26ff57841cb9f4bfb5a1ff6780a5f199e7d254.png

That’s all for now! We’ll be sharing more progress as we go, but in the meantime you can follow us for updates on Twitter or join the community in our brand new Discord channel.

notes.title: Our First Development Update, UI Reveal & Character Spotlight
notes.notes:
Hey everyone! I’m Adam from Robust Games, and I’m excited to be kicking off the Loco Motive development blog! It’s going to be a fun journey, and we’re excited for players to be able to see what we’re working on behind the scenes.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/2fc379384bdac7f7b9cfd1d841c5d5885d7779c5.png

Development Update

Before we get into our first character spotlight, we wanted to chat a little about how development is going since our announcement a few months back.

The story has been written, the puzzles have been designed and mapped out. A large portion of the game is fully playable, we’re currently working hard on cramming in gorgeous pixel art, plenty of beautifully animated hijinks, and the snappiest of snappy dialogue!

Shiny New UI

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/c6b7f6b1e241a70359de6a54c30d7ca4fc572639.png

We brought award winning UI Artist, Edd Coates onto the team. Edd has knocked it out of the park with a contemporary high resolution interface that blends in seamlessly with traditional pixel art.

By taking inspiration from other fantastic point and click titles, we have designed an interface that is both elegant and intuitive to use.  For those of you looking forward to playing this on the Switch, we took an enormous amount of care to ensure that the game is just as fun to play in docked/gamepad mode as it is with a mouse or touch screen.

Combined with the fantastic user experience, Edd has opted to go with an Art Deco theme that’s reminiscent of 20s to 30s architecture.  This will adorn the many screens and menus that you’ll be seeing in-game, to give it that classic ‘Gatsby vibe’ and really ground the UI in the world of Loco Motive.

We’ve also got some lovely new screenshots to share, see below!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/1609de365c2f62488e57d2a8020eb7500bde0622.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/48ee4c8fcf197b4710eba91ff812fbe93a00eca6.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/ae0b3bd407dec7ed208ae0378cd5ac7878fa3418.png

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/696181bfdf8220abe835d47729e87b28fcc12ddb.png

Character Spotlight - Arthur A. Ackerman

The characters are at the heart of Loco Motive – a cast of exciting and energetic characters who each have their own distinct personalities and motivations. Here’s a look at the first of our characters.

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/fca3dc3c88c2d16b9d2dbe7620d8564a8dd343b9.png

Arthur Ackerman is an otherwise straight-laced lawyer, someone who perhaps is defined as 'by the books'. Employed by Lady Unterwald to handle some last minute amendments to her will, she encourages him to have a good time while he's aboard her flagship train, the Reuss Express. 

Arthur's idea of a good time involves looking at paperwork, but he soon becomes embroiled in the mysterious murder of his employer. Stuck aboard the Reuss Express and with his life potentially on the line, Arthur is on an adventure - whether he likes it or not!

{STEAM_CLAN_IMAGE}/41650287/b6089eaacd9b752e088f905aee9446e2d163d0b2.png

That’s all for now! We’ll be sharing more progress as we go on our Twitter and you can find us hanging out in the Chucklefish Discord - come say hi! 

Until next time!

- Adam
